title.en: Wisdom Paves the Way (play): knowledge and wisdom

text.en: Four young men, Ram Datt, Shiv Datt, Har Datt and Dev Datt, walk to the city of Ujjain looking for work.

This is a short play, so it has characters, a setting and stage directions in brackets.
The characters include the King of Ujjain, four young men, a merchant and two sentries.
The first setting is a dusty road to Ujjain, and later the king's court decorated with rich tapestries and tall pillars.
The young men are tired and determined, and they have been walking for ten days in search of work.
The title tells us the theme: wisdom, which is knowing how to use what you know, helps people more than knowledge alone.
Knowledge is the facts and skills we learn, while wisdom is good judgement in using them.
Before reading, the book asks us to classify examples, like someone who values time with family over chasing wealth, as wisdom.
Stage directions describe actions, and a play shows its story only through dialogue and action.
Words to learn: resolute means determined, bustling means busy, and eludes means is difficult to obtain.
Read the play aloud with friends, giving each character its own voice.

problem.en: Classify: a student knows many facts about plants. Another uses that knowledge to grow vegetables and share with neighbours.

text.en: Wisdom is knowledge used with good judgement.

prompt.en: What is the difference between knowledge and wisdom?

points.en: A play has characters, settings and stage directions.
Wisdom is good judgement; knowledge is facts.
